parts:
turn this into an explantion i can say to the belle girls: What changed in each document.
In the Memberships, every tier now carries a GLP-1 and peptide discount that matches its treatment percentage: 10, 15, 20, and 25 percent up the ladder. The intro and the "How It Works" section now say member pricing covers wellness too, and the VIP annual credit example can be redeemed as a peptide cycle.
In the Packages, there's a new Wellness and Longevity section. GLP-1 runs as quarterly Belle Body Reset programs built straight off Belle's vial prices, three vials at a 10 to 14 percent bundle saving. Peptides carry your menu names with per-cycle pricing, single peptides from $200 to $400 and signature stacks from $450 to $525, with a 12 percent saving for a three-cycle commitment. The Signature Year now has a real wellness track you can fold into the monthly payment, and the Good to Know section spells out that tier discounts apply to à la carte wellness but not to the already-discounted programs.
Two things to confirm, since they decide whether wellness prints money the way the rest of the menu does.
The peptide prices are market averages, not Belle's. I used current clinic pricing, single peptides around $200 to $400 per cycle and the BPC-157 and TB-500 stacks around $450 to $525, because Belle gave names without numbers. Stronger version: get Belle's actual compounding pharmacy cost per peptide and reset these against real margin, the same way we did with tox and filler. Until then, treat them as placeholders.
The discount choice you made, same percent as treatments, is the one spot that bites on refills. On a once-a-month GLP-1 buy, 25 percent VIP off a $549 tirzepatide vial is about $137 every month, roughly $1,644 a year of margin given to a single VIP member, and the entry semaglutide vial at 25 percent off is the thinnest line once you net out pharmacy cost. It still clears at typical costs, but it is the least protected number in the build. Stronger version: cap the wellness discount at 15 percent, or switch it to a flat member vial rate, which keeps the loyalty hook without bleeding on every refill. Say the word and I'll flip it.

Here's a simple way to explain it to the Belle team:

"After reviewing the memberships and packages, we made a few strategic updates to better integrate wellness and longevity services into the same ecosystem as your aesthetic treatments.

On the membership side, we aligned the GLP-1 and peptide discounts with each membership tier. So as patients move up the ladder, they receive 10%, 15%, 20%, and 25% savings respectively. We also updated the language throughout the membership program to make it clear that member pricing applies not only to treatments, but also to wellness services. Even the VIP annual credit can now be used toward peptide programs, which gives members more flexibility and increases the perceived value of the membership.

On the package side, we added an entirely new Wellness & Longevity section. This includes your Belle Body Reset GLP-1 programs, structured as quarterly programs based on your vial pricing, along with peptide programs and signature peptide stacks. We built in commitment incentives so patients save money when they commit to multiple cycles, while still protecting profitability.

We also incorporated wellness into the Signature Year package, allowing patients to bundle aesthetics, wellness, and longevity into one comprehensive program rather than viewing them as separate purchases. The goal is to increase patient lifetime value and create a more complete transformation journey.

There are just two areas I'd like us to confirm before finalizing.

First, the peptide pricing currently reflects industry averages because we didn't have Belle's exact compounding pharmacy costs. The structure is solid, but once we have your actual costs, we can optimize pricing the same way we would with tox, filler, or laser services to ensure maximum profitability.

Second, I want us to revisit the wellness discount percentages. Matching the membership discount to wellness sounds great from a patient perspective, but at the highest VIP level, a 25% discount on recurring GLP-1 refills can start to erode margin over time. It still works, but it's the weakest profitability point in the entire build.

My recommendation would be either capping wellness discounts at 15% regardless of membership tier or moving to a flat member pricing model for GLP-1s and peptides. Patients still feel like they're getting an exclusive benefit, but it protects thousands of dollars in annual margin per patient.

Overall, the framework is strong. These changes create a much better bridge between aesthetics, wellness, and longevity while increasing retention, recurring revenue, and patient lifetime value. We just need to fine-tune the wellness pricing to make sure it's as profitable as the rest of the business."
